solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Morning exam not distinguishing right from wrong (6)

blocks.note: an oral is a spoken exam

annotation.surface: A candidate sits a morning test and can't tell right answers from wrong ones.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'right from wrong' sound like marking an exam; it is really about morality.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the prefix a- means without, so amoral is lacking any moral sense, rather than choosing wrong.

entries.clue: Show program feature used for sound capture (6)

blocks.note: an app is a software program
the ear is the facial feature that catches sound

annotation.surface: A software feature for recording audio, as in a phone app's microphone setting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' reads as a noun, a TV programme; it is the verb, to turn up. 'Feature' is a part of the face.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym of the verb: to show, as in 'he didn't show', means to turn up.

entries.clue: Rash developing as very hot (9)

indicatorNotes.developing: letters developing change into a new form

annotation.surface: A skin rash that flares up when the weather is very hot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint; it is the adjective meaning reckless.
annotation.definitionFit: A rash decision is one made overhastily, without thought.

entries.clue: Don’t go near an empty space (5)

blocks.note: an empty space or vacuum, as in 'staring into the ___'

annotation.surface: A warning to keep away from a gaping hole.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an instruction, and AVOID works as an instruction too: 'Avoid an empty space'.
annotation.definitionFit: To avoid something is to keep away from it.

entries.clue: Part of family includes one mastermind (6)

indicatorNotes.includes: the first piece includes the second inside it

blocks.note: in biology a family is divided into genera, so a genus is part of a family

annotation.surface: One member of the family is the clever one who plans everything.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Family' is the biological rank, not relatives. GEN(I)US.
annotation.definitionFit: A mastermind is a person of great intellect, a genius.

entries.clue: How far one can hear others running round area (7)

indicatorNotes.round: the jumbled letters go round the other piece

annotation.surface: Something about how far a person can hear other people jogging round a district.
annotation.walkthrough: The A goes in after the first letter: E(A)RSHOT.
annotation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range within which a sound can be heard.

entries.clue: What sounds like fashionable pub (3)

indicatorNotes.What sounds like: says outright that the answer is said like the next word

blocks.note: in = fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

annotation.surface: Asking what a trendy bar sounds like.
annotation.walkthrough: IN and INN are pronounced the same.
annotation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub, often one offering rooms.

entries.clue: Revamped store installing European sound system (6)

indicatorNotes.Revamped: a revamped thing has been remade, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.installing: the rearranged letters have the other piece installed inside them

annotation.surface: A refurbished shop fitting a new European sound system.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a shop refit; the E goes in near the end: STER(E)O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word, short for stereophonic, came to name the home hi-fi itself.

entries.clue: Majority of English think about splitting trip (13)

indicatorNotes.splitting: the first pieces split the last one in two by going inside it

blocks.note: to ponder is to think about something
to trip is to step lightly, to prance

annotation.surface: Most English people mulling over a split in their journey.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trip' looks like a journey but is the verb for skipping along. 'About' belongs with 'think'. PR(E PONDER)ANCE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means outweighing, so a preponderance of votes is the larger share.

entries.clue: Troublemaking from 500 bad people over time (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, the earlier pieces sit over the last

annotation.surface: Mischief caused by five hundred bad people over a period of time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over time' reads as 'eventually'; here it places the T below the rest in a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: Devilment is mischievous or wild behaviour, troublemaking.

entries.clue: A research degree about island insect (5)

indicatorNotes.about: the degree goes about, round, the island letter

blocks.note: a PhD is a doctorate by research

annotation.surface: A doctorate thesis about an insect found on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: A + PH(I)D.
annotation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect such as the greenfly.

entries.clue: Clive moved around Delhi regularly in wheeled transport (7)

indicatorNotes.moved: Clive's letters are moved into a new order
indicatorNotes.around: the rearranged letters go around the other piece
indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at regular intervals: the 2nd and 4th

annotation.surface: A man called Clive travelling around Delhi often, in some wheeled contraption.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like 'often' but picks every other letter of Delhi. V(EH)ICLE.
annotation.definitionFit: A vehicle is anything with wheels used for transport.

entries.clue: Happy having home in Asia? (9)

indicatorNotes.having: the first word has the second within it

annotation.surface: Someone content to be living in Asia.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: Asia is one continent. CONT(IN)ENT.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: Asia is the largest of the seven continents.

entries.clue: Silly small child gave the game away (9)

annotation.definitionNote: Silly here is the noun, as in 'you silly', a foolish person

blocks.note: s = small, as on clothing labels
an imp is a mischievous child
to let on is to reveal a secret

annotation.surface: A foolish little child blurted out the secret.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like an adjective describing the child; it is the noun, a silly person.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym of the noun: 'you silly' calls someone a fool, which is what a simpleton is.

entries.clue: A German promoting male executive (7)

indicatorNotes.promoting: in a down clue, promoting a piece moves it up, above the rest

annotation.surface: A German boss giving a man a promotion at work.
annotation.walkthrough: The office picture of promotion hides a placement instruction: MAN goes above A GER.
annotation.definitionFit: A manager is an executive who runs part of a business.

entries.clue: Peculiar child very likely to succeed (4-2)

annotation.surface: An eccentric child who is a sure bet to do well.
annotation.definitionFit: An odds-on favourite is expected to win.
annotation.walkthrough: In betting, odds-on means the stake exceeds the potential winnings, because the outcome is expected.

entries.clue: Tricky problem getting energy into police weapon (6)

indicatorNotes.into: one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: a Taser is an electric stun gun used by police

annotation.surface: A technical difficulty in getting power into a police stun gun.
annotation.walkthrough: T(E)ASER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brain-teaser is a puzzle, and teaser alone carries the sense.

entries.clue: Prominent female you once found in metaphysical poet (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: one piece is found inside the other

blocks.note: ye is an old form of you
John Donne, the best-known metaphysical poet

annotation.surface: A leading woman discovered in the poems of a metaphysical writer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals an archaic word. DO(YE)NNE.
annotation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected or prominent woman in a field.

entries.clue: Use credit card to steal (5)

blocks.note: to run a card through a reader to pay
informal for to pinch or nick something

annotation.surface: Card fraud: using someone's credit card in order to steal.
annotation.definitionFit: Swipe means both to pass a card through a reader and to pinch something.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface joins the two senses into one crime, so the card-theft picture hides that each half is its own definition.

entries.clue: Cut tail off the bird (5)

indicatorNotes.tail off: the tail of a word is its last letter, taken off it

annotation.surface: An instruction to trim the tail feathers from a bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut tail off' looks like a deletion; 'Cut' is SNIP, and 'tail off the' gives the E at the end of 'the'.
annotation.definitionFit: The snipe is a wading bird with a long bill.

entries.clue: Energy in branch high tension cables beginning to short (13)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: take the beginning, the first letter, of the next word

blocks.note: a sprig is a small branch
HT = high tension, the electrical abbreviation

annotation.surface: A power-grid report: energy in a branch line whose high-voltage cables are starting to short-circuit.
annotation.walkthrough: The electrical picture makes 'Energy' look like power; it means liveliness. 'Branch' is part of a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of vigour: sprightly means lively and full of energy.

entries.clue: Boring routine in truth (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies in the next word

annotation.surface: A dull daily grind contains a kernel of truth.
annotation.definitionFit: Being in a rut means stuck in a dull routine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' tells you the answer is sitting inside the next word; the definition is the whole phrase 'Boring routine'.

entries.clue: Kind of a tuner needing adjustment (6)

indicatorNotes.needing adjustment: the letters need to be adjusted into a new order

annotation.surface: A sort of radio tuner that needs fiddling with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'sort of'; 'Kind' is the noun, as in 'things of that nature'.
annotation.definitionFit: Nature can mean kind or type: 'of a serious nature'.

entries.clue: Character who’s renting property (6)

blocks.note: a symbol of the alphabet, such as A or B
one who lets out a house or flat: let + -er

annotation.surface: A colourful landlord type who rents out houses.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person; it is a written symbol. 'Renting' is renting out: to let.
annotation.definitionFit: Letters are the characters of an alphabet, and a letter is also one who lets.
